index.intro: An independent, evidence-led guide to Michaela: who has taught there, what is documented about learning, what the results mean, and what still needs checking. Updated 21 October 2026.

blocks.title: Why the first page was incomplete
body: The first HTML page was built from the initial four-row placeholder. The larger historical register was not connected to it. That was an implementation failure, not evidence that the additional research did not exist.

This release restores all 85 name entries and applies dated corrections from the recovered biographies. The count includes fellows, surname-only records and possible duplicates. It does not certify a complete employee census.

blocks.title: Keep three decisions separate
body: Attainment: judge results by exam year, subject entries and pupil context, not headline percentages alone. Admission: a non-academically-selective school can still be heavily oversubscribed. Suitability: consider the child's response to routines, workload and breadth as well as grades.
The home-learning page is our adaptation. It is not the school's proprietary scheme of work and does not guarantee grade 9s.

blocks.title: Research coverage and remaining unknowns
blocks.status: Published evidence, not an official school prospectus
body: The historical staff reconstruction is substantially fuller than the first page, but many exact employment dates and current jobs are not public. The current school website and some archives were inaccessible on re-check; recovered source extracts are labelled accordingly.

The complete current Year 7 weekly timetable, every subject's year-by-year scheme and the 2028 admissions policy have not been verified here. Those gaps are shown rather than filled with guesses. Book previews are not labelled as free full books.

curriculum.intro: The useful question is not just which books pupils read, but how knowledge is sequenced, explained, practised, checked and revisited. Historical examples are not a promise of the 2026/27 timetable.

blocks.title: What independent inspection actually observed
body: In May 2023, inspectors described a broad curriculum, frequent recall, checks on understanding and prompt correction of misconceptions. They gave a concrete sequence: Year 8 learning about the Russian Revolution supported Year 9 work on Cold War ideologies. Daily reading and support for weaker readers were also observed.

blocks.title: Subject content: an evidence map
body: This is a map of documented examples, not a complete current scheme. Content can change; a topic appearing in GCSE results does not prove every child is offered it.

rows: English
Rich literature, including older and contemporary texts; explicit vocabulary and substantial reading. Early published accounts include Greek myths, the Odyssey and Julius Caesar in Year 7.
Early book list is historical; current year-by-year reading list needs school confirmation.
Maths
Fluency and cumulative knowledge are prominent in staff writing. The register documents Maths and Further Maths sixth-form specialists.
A complete KS3/KS4 sequence and the current exam board are not verified by those biographies.
Science
Separate disciplinary teaching can sit inside a Combined Science GCSE route. Current retained results show a large Combined Science cohort and a small separate-science cohort.
Three science disciplines does not automatically mean three GCSEs; do not assume AQA or universal triple science.
History
Chronology and substantive knowledge; the 2023 inspection records Russian Revolution in Year 8 feeding Cold War work in Year 9.
Examples are not a full national-history specification.
Geography / religion
The 2020 staff book has curriculum accounts by Grace Steggall and Sarah James.
Read the original accounts for detail; publishing a chapter in 2020 does not establish present employment or an unchanged syllabus.
French
Grammar, vocabulary and repeated practice appear in Jess Lund's teaching accounts. A 27 November 2022 post still describes French teaching, including Year 12.
Use dated lesson accounts as examples, not a complete current GCSE specification.
Art / music / sport
Inspection recorded musical and sporting clubs and visits, alongside formal curriculum provision.
There is no basis here to say Michaela has no arts or sport. Exact weekly hours, instruments, teams and DT opportunities need current confirmation.

blocks.title: Timetable: known limits, not an invented grid
body: No current, fully sourced Year 7 subject-by-subject weekly timetable has been established. The earlier research contained historical lesson lengths and homework totals, but those do not safely establish the current day.

Directory reproductions conflict on science allocation: one gives four hours, another five. They may describe different periods or contain errors. Neither is treated as the authoritative 2026/27 timetable.
blocks.question: Please share a current Year 7 timetable, lesson length, homework schedule, club timetable and the taught hours for art, music, PE and DT. Which arrangements will apply to the intended entry year?

blocks.title: How the knowledge-organiser approach works
body: Joe Kirby's March 2015 account describes selecting essential knowledge, making it explicit and revisiting it through retrieval. He also stresses explaining, sequencing, combining and practising knowledge: a facts sheet is a support, not the whole education.

At home, a useful check has three parts: recall the fact; explain it in your own words; use it on a new question. A child who recites an answer but cannot transfer it needs further teaching, not simply a larger flashcard pile.

blocks.title: Resources to use alongside school work
body: Use the national curriculum to audit coverage, then match later GCSE practice to the actual awarding body and specification. Do not purchase a full AQA course solely because a directory or a previous assistant assumed that board.

results.intro: Read grade distributions alongside entries, prior attainment and pupil context. The figures below come from Openday's retained dataset rather than replacing it with a new headline.

blocks.title: What these results do not prove
blocks.status: Exam year, publication version and denominator matter
body: A school-wide grade 9 rate is not the probability that a particular child will get a 9, and it is not the proportion of children achieving all 9s. Progress 8 is a school-level comparison with pupils with similar prior attainment, not a controlled experiment isolating the teaching method.

The latest stored subject series is labelled 2025/26 provisional. The hub uses that label rather than the stale 2024/25 wording in one legacy method string. It does not use the misleading legacy grade9to7AllGCSE field as an all-entry top-grade rate. Historical records remain unchanged.

concerns.intro: A critical assessment should help a family make a decision, not collect hostile claims. This page separates established events, attributed criticism, the school's rationale and unresolved questions.

blocks.title: Strict routines: benefit for some, strain for others
body: Reporting in TIME in 2018 described silent transitions, close attention to posture and sanctions for small rule breaches. Critics questioned autonomy and creativity; supporters saw calm classrooms and stronger learning. This is dated reporting, not a measurement of every pupil's experience.
For balance, the May 2023 inspection described positive staff-pupil relationships and pupils feeling safe. A positive inspection does not establish that every child finds the culture comfortable.
blocks.question: How are genuine mistakes, anxiety, SEND needs and repeated difficulties handled? What reasonable adjustments can a child actually receive, and how can pupils raise a concern?

blocks.title: Prayer policy: distinguish the ruling from a value judgement
blocks.status: Dated legal event; not legal advice or a claim about subsequent litigation
body: On 16 April 2024 the High Court rejected the challenge to the school's prayer-ritual policy. The pupil argued that the restriction burdened religious practice; the school argued for cohesion and a consistent secular environment. Upholding a policy does not mean all families must consider it suitable.

The same proceedings also found that one five-day suspension had been procedurally unfair because the pupil had not been given an opportunity to give her account. Reporting the case simply as an unqualified school victory omits that separate finding.
blocks.question: What is the current written policy on religious observance, and how are pupil representations heard before sanctions?

blocks.title: Breadth and opportunity: ask for quantities
body: The missing current timetable prevents a robust comparison with schools offering extensive music, art, DT and sport. Do not substitute either the claim that Michaela has no enrichment or the claim that every child can access everything.

A practical comparison needs taught minutes, regular participation, rehearsal and competition opportunities, facilities, selection rules and clashes. Ask what happens to children who do not volunteer or need encouragement to join.
blocks.question: Can you show an ordinary pupil's actual term of music, art, making/design and sport, not just examples involving the most active pupils?

blocks.title: Workload, conformity and family fit
body: A highly structured school can reduce uncertainty, but a family should still test whether the child will accept the routines and the homework. Ask how long work actually takes weaker, middle and stronger attainers, and what happens when a pupil tries hard but cannot finish.
The staff books defend authority, a shared culture and a deliberately selected curriculum. These are the school's arguments, not independent proof that alternative educational philosophies fail.
blocks.question: How do teachers distinguish lack of understanding from lack of effort? How often is work adapted, and how is progress discussed with parents?

blocks.title: Claims that this evidence does not justify
body: The historical name list cannot establish a turnover rate: the underlying website pages cover different groups. A degree in another field does not prove poor teaching or a lack of subject training. Missing current employment information does not prove unemployment.

Exceptional GCSE results alone do not identify which elements of the school caused them. A useful assessment also checks entry patterns, prior attainment, admissions rules, pupil movement and outcomes beyond exams. No unsupported allegation of pupil removal or manipulation is made here.

blocks.status: Formats checked 21 October 2026; no full free PDF claimed
body: The publisher lists an ebook edition (ISBN 9781913808549). Hive explicitly lists a DRM-protected EPUB. OverDrive provides a library-search route; availability depends on library membership and holdings.

The 41-page authorised PDF preview includes contents and chapter summaries. For practical follow-up in the full book, use the curriculum and teaching sections: history starts at printed page 167, geography at 181, religious education at 189, questioning at 345, feedback at 359 and knowledge organisers at 373. These full chapters are not all included in the preview.

blocks.status: PDF / EPUB availability unresolved; no pirate download links
body: The print edition is ISBN 9781909717961. A specific lawful full PDF or EPUB for this first book was not verified in this research. The library catalogue entry is a finding aid, not a promise that an ebook can be borrowed.

Use the print edition or ask a library to locate that ISBN. The 2020 follow-up is readily identifiable as an authorised EPUB; do not confuse it with the first book or with Amy Chua's different book, Battle Hymn of the Tiger Mother.

blocks.title: Read in this order
body: First: read a dated classroom account and the inspection report to see what is actually described. Second: use the book contents to choose a subject and teaching chapter. Third: write one small home experiment and an observable success check. Finally: read the concerns page and ask what evidence would change your view.
Keep a note of which edition, date and author supports each idea. A teacher's 2015 account is useful historical evidence; it is not automatically the school's current policy.

history.intro: Preserve the evidence, not just the latest website. Archive snapshots record what was published on a particular day; they do not establish who was employed on every intervening day.

blocks.title: Research release history
body: The initial workbook and web page contained four people. The separate 85-entry reconstruction was subsequently restored to staff.json on 21 October 2026. This release connects the full data to the page, adds the recovered qualification corrections, sources and research sections, and adds automated coverage checks.

The original data file is retained. staff-corrections.json records field-level amendments and new sources. Every rendered record and CSV export applies those same amendments, so information is not stranded in a research note.

blocks.title: How future significant changes should be recorded
body: Keep a dated source URL or exact archive capture, state what changed, retain the previous record and identify whether it is a school announcement, independent report or inference. Change an employment date only when a source establishes it.

Website redesigns and edited pages should be recorded as such. Do not upload complete commercial books or mirror whole third-party sites without permission. This release provides a curated history, not an automated archive-monitoring service.

alternatives.intro: Treat Michaela as a desirable but uncertain admission route. Build a portfolio in which at least one option is realistically accessible, rather than replacing one oversubscribed school with several others.

blocks.title: Michaela: non-selective is not guaranteed
body: Michaela does not select Year 7 pupils by academic entrance test. Previous arrangements use oversubscription priorities and random allocation for the relevant local-distance group. The exact entry-year rules must be read before treating any distance or lottery claim as current.

For a pupil in Year 5 during 2026/27, ordinary Year 7 entry is September 2028. Do not use the 2026 or 2027 policy as though it were the determined 2028 policy. The routine state-secondary application deadline is 31 October of Year 6, but check the local authority's published 2028 timetable when issued.

A reported last-offer distance at a lottery school is not a conventional guaranteed catchment radius. Applications divided by places are not an individual probability: priority groups, preferences, offers elsewhere and waiting-list movement matter.
blocks.question: For the intended year, what is the published admission number, ordered priority list, random-allocation group and waiting-list method?

blocks.title: A realistic alternative-school shortlist
body: These are research candidates, not schools for which eligibility or an offer has been confirmed. Use Openday's admissions and performance records together, then check the official policy for the intended year. A school with strong results but an inaccessible admission route is not a safety net.

rows: Local non-selective baseline
Whitmore; other eligible Harrow or neighbouring-borough schools
Address/priority eligibility and actual offer history must be checked; proximity is not assumed.
Other non-selective high-attainment possibilities

blocks.title: Use a two-stage decision
body: First screen admission feasibility: applicable year, real address/priority eligibility, assessment requirements, affordable total cost and journey. Only then rank likely educational fit and provision. Keep one genuinely plausible route even when pursuing more ambitious choices.

For each finalist, compare the same evidence: grade 9 and grades 9-7 by exam year; subject choices; progress where available; support for middle attainers; homework; teacher stability with caveats; and ordinary participation in music, art, DT and sport.
blocks.question: What evidence shows that a child entering around national-average attainment can make strong progress here, and what support and enrichment would that particular child actually receive?

blocks.title: Keep enrichment independent of the school outcome
body: A family can preserve regular ensemble music, instrument lessons, sport and making/art opportunities whatever the school allocation. That is a planning strategy, not a claim that an external activity is identical to another school's provision.
Choose a manageable weekly mix, leave recovery time, and check travel. The home-learning plan should strengthen foundations rather than consume all the time available for interests and friendship.

home-learning.intro: A practical adaptation for an upper-primary child, not a claim to reproduce Michaela at home. Start with understanding and sustainable habits; GCSE grade 9 is a long-term aspiration, not a promised outcome.

blocks.title: Start tomorrow: a 25-minute session
body: Use an existing school topic to avoid creating a second competing curriculum. Spend 5 minutes recalling earlier learning without notes, 8 minutes on one explanation and worked example, 8 minutes on independent questions, then 4 minutes correcting and explaining one error. Add ordinary shared or independent reading separately.

Stop or reduce the session when attention or frustration makes practice unproductive. Accuracy, explanation and retention matter more than speed alone. Keep music, sport, sleep and play protected. The timings are our suggested starting point, not a Michaela policy.

blocks.title: A worked example: fractions, not rote tricks
blocks.status: Original teaching example and model answers; adapt difficulty to the child
body: Ask: What does 3/4 mean? Why is it equal to 6/8? A sound explanation is that the same whole has been divided into twice as many equal pieces, so twice as many pieces are needed.

Model 3/4 + 1/8 by rewriting 3/4 as 6/8, then adding to get 7/8. Ask the child to explain why 3/4 + 1/8 is not 4/12. The denominators describe the size of pieces, so unlike pieces cannot simply be counted together.

Independent checks: 1/2 + 3/8 = 7/8; 5/6 - 1/3 = 1/2; 3/4 of 20 = 15. Transfer check: a jug is 3/4 full and 1/8 of its full capacity is poured out: 5/8 remains. Revisit one similar question the next day and one a week later.

blocks.title: Reading: build knowledge and use evidence
blocks.status: Original example; not an excerpt from a copyrighted book
body: Read a short section from the child's current book. Choose at most three unfamiliar words; explain each in context, then ask for a new sentence. Next ask one literal question, one inference and one summary.

Example invented sentence: "Amir paused at the dark doorway, then tightened his grip on the torch." Literal: where did he pause? At the doorway. Inference: he may be apprehensive; pausing and gripping the torch more tightly support that reading, though the sentence does not explicitly name his feeling. Summary: Amir hesitates before entering.

On the following day, ask for the words and a short account without reopening the text. Accept a well-supported alternative inference; the aim is reasoning from evidence, not memorising a parent's preferred answer.

blocks.title: Four weeks, with a decision at the end
body: Use the child's own schoolwork as the content source. The table is a suggested experiment. Do not add all subjects every night.

rows: Choose one arithmetic gap and one reading goal. Use four short sessions.
A dated baseline of 8-10 questions, one reading response and the child's explanation.
Revisit the same ideas using new numbers/texts; teach one small extension.
Which errors recur? Can the child explain without prompts?
Mix old and new questions; include one unfamiliar application.
Separate remembered facts from successful transfer.
Repeat an equivalent, not identical, check after a gap. Review workload together.
Compare accuracy, independence, explanation and enjoyment. Continue, simplify or change the method.

blocks.title: A small error log that changes the next lesson
body: Record only date, question/topic, error type, correction and next review date. Useful error types are: did not know; misunderstood; chose the wrong method; arithmetic slip; misread the question.

For a misunderstood concept, reteach with a different example. For a retrieval gap, use a short later quiz. For a misread question, practise identifying exactly what is requested. Do not prescribe the same extra worksheet for every mistake.
A possible review schedule is next day, three days, one week and a month. Adjust it to demonstrated retention; these are planning intervals, not a uniquely proven Michaela formula.
links: EEF guidance on planning and checking learning

blocks.title: From primary foundations to eventual GCSE depth
body: Years 5-6: secure reading, vocabulary, number sense, fractions, writing and curiosity. Years 7-9: follow the actual school curriculum, add cumulative retrieval and extended answers, and identify misconceptions early. Years 10-11: match practice to the actual specification, mark schemes and examiner expectations, including unfamiliar applications.

A grade 9 requires more than flashcards: accurate knowledge, connected understanding, interpretation, sustained reasoning and performance across the assessed content. Use timed exam practice when appropriate, not as the default activity for a nine- or ten-year-old.
